max_tire.note: Owners call 31 in the practical ceiling and 30x9.50s a known-good fit; one long-time owner ran 32x11.50s on stock springs with minor rubbing. Test-fit, since actual diameters vary
A 2.5 in spring lift plus 3/4 in shackles runs 32s without trouble; 33s fit until the suspension stuffs. Narrow-track CJs need the steering stops reset or the tires hit the leaf springs
Usually with flares and trimmed rear wheel openings; 33–35s generally mean cutting the rear openings and revisiting the bump stops

items.title: Electronic ignition wire connectors
items.summary: Connectors could not carry enough current for the electronic ignition control.

items.title: Transmission adapter-plate seal
items.summary: A mis-seated seal could let gear oil migrate from the manual transmission into the transfer case.

items.title: Intermediate steering-shaft coupling
items.summary: Oversized serrations could stop the coupling clamping properly to the steering-gear shaft.

items.title: Tie-rod adjuster clamp bolts
items.summary: Loose clamp bolts could shift the steering-wheel position and risk loss of steering.

items.title: Transmission-to-transfer-case gasket
items.summary: Wrong gasket could block lubricant flow and damage the manual transmission.

items.title: Rear seat-belt buckles missing
items.summary: Some Jeeps got two tongue-end rear belt halves and no buckle.

items.title: Manual transmission first-gear lubrication
items.summary: Factory-fill gear oil might not protect first gear.

timeline.change: Willys CJ-5 arrives on an 81 in wheelbase, derived from the Korean War M38A1, with the 134 cu in Hurricane four
Optional Perkins 192 cu in diesel four (62 hp); Tuxedo Park trim lines run 1961–64

Buick-designed 225 cu in Dauntless V6 (155 hp) becomes optional; by 1968 about 75% of CJ-5s have it. Jeep-CJ.com calls the 1966–71 Dauntless desirable, strong and reliable. 'Jeep CJ-5' replaces 'Willys' after 1964
AMC era begins (bought Kaiser Jeep in 1970); last Buick V6 year; Trac-Lok replaces Powr-Lok; PTOs dropped

AMC 232/258 sixes and optional 304 V8; wheelbase stretched 2.5 in to 83.5 in, nose 5 in longer, open-knuckle Dana 30 front, fuel tank behind the rear axle. Hagerty's pick is an AMC-era 232 or 258 six from 1972 on
Revised frame and more rounded tub; new windshield angle, so 1955–75 tops don't fit; AMC 20 two-piece-shaft rear replaces the Dana 44
Fully boxed frame; power disc brakes, air conditioning and the Golden Eagle package become options
258 six with two-barrel Carter BBD becomes standard; 1,000-unit Silver Anniversary edition

GM 151 Iron Duke four becomes standard with an SR4 four-speed (Jeep-CJ.com calls the Iron Duke a particularly weak engine to avoid); the 258 option gets the T-176 four-speed; locking hubs change to a five-bolt pattern (1980 per Wikipedia, 1981 per Offroaders.com). 1983 is the last year

identify.intro: Twenty-nine years of CJ-5 means three body generations, five engine families and a flood of postal and Willys parts trucks, so date the tub before you trust the title.

items.head: Early vs late body
items.body: 1955–75: 81 in wheelbase (83.5 in from 1972), 59 in windshield, windshield retainer welded on, windshield at 90° to the hood, no factory door hinges. 1976–83: 55 in sloped windshield with screw-on retainer, factory roll bar and door hinges, 83.5 in wheelbase, about 71.5 in from door hinge to the rear of the tub.

items.head: CJ-5 vs CJ-6 vs DJ-5
items.body: A CJ-6 is the same Jeep with a longer rear tub (101 in wheelbase to 1971, then 103.5 in per Wikipedia; Quadratec says 103 in). DJ-5 Dispatchers are two-wheel-drive postal Jeeps, so check for a front driveshaft and driven front axle.

items.head: VIN format
items.body: 1971–80 CJs use a 13-character Jeep VIN; 1981–83 trucks use the 17-character federal VIN, where characters 6–7 read 85 for a CJ-5, the 4th character is the engine (B = 151 four, C = 258 six, H = 304 V8) and the 10th the model year (B = 1981, C = 1982, D = 1983).

items.head: VIN plate vs frame
items.body: The main VIN tag is riveted to the driver's side firewall; compare it with the partial VIN stamped on the passenger-side frame rail above the rear wheel. A mismatch can mean a swapped tub or salvage history.

items.head: Real Renegades
items.body: From 1972 the Renegade package meant the 304 V8, alloy wheels and a Trac-Lok rear. A six-cylinder 'Renegade' with steel wheels is either re-engined or wearing borrowed stripes.

values.intro: Still the cheapest way into a classic CJ: the CJ-5 trails the CJ-7 by several thousand dollars, and only clean, original V8 trucks and tidy restorations break $25k.
values.note: Compiled from Bring a Trailer CJ-5 results in October 2026 (about 67 sales of Willys and Jeep CJ-5s, median around $10,500, middle half roughly $7,000–16,000). Recheck current results before relying on these figures.
